canonical_question: What is the measured hardness of the as-deposited CuMoTaWV refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) film, and how does it quantitatively compare to the hardness of the referenced nanocrystalline NbMoTaW RHEA film?

question_variants.question: How does the penetration depth being kept below 10% of the film thickness ensure that substrate effects did not influence the measured hardness of 19.5 GPa?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text states the condition (penetration depth <10% of thickness) was met but does not explicitly link this criterion to the exclusion of substrate effects for the measured hardness value.
source_evidence_spans: The penetration depth is kept below 10% of the RHEA film thickness.

question_variants.question: How does the hardness of the new CuMoTaWV film compare quantitatively to the 12 GPa reported by Kim et al. for the NbMoTaW film?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text provides the hardness of the CuMoTaWV film as 19 GPa (with uncertainty 2.3 GPa) and references the 12 GPa hardness of the NbMoTaW film by Kim et al. This allows for a direct quantitative comparison.

answers.answer: The hardness of the new CuMoTaWV film is 19 GPa, which is higher than the 12 GPa reported for the nanocrystalline NbMoTaW RHEA film. The text states: 'The target was used to sputter a nanocrystalline RHEA film... The hardness... value: 19, unit: GPa' and references the 'nanocrystalline NbMoTaW RHEA film that showed a hardness of 12 GPa' in the context of the question or related literature discussion.
answers.mechanism: Solid solution hardening and grain boundary strengthening.
evidence_spans: In this work, a refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) film of equimolar CuMoTaWV was deposited on silicon and 304 stainless-steel substrates using DC-magnetron sputtering.
A sputtering target was developed by partial sintering of an equimolar powder mixture of Cu, Mo, Ta, W, and V using spark plasma sintering.
The target was used to sputter a nanocrystalline RHEA film with a thickness of ∼900 nm and an average grain size of 18 nm.

source_evidence_spans: nanocrystalline NbMoTaW RHEA film that showed a hardness of 12 GPa

cross_paper_synthesis.contradictions: No direct contradictions exist within the provided text. cross_paper_synthesis.candidate_hypothesis: The addition of Copper (Cu) and Vanadium (V) to the Mo-Ta-W base, forming the CuMoTaWV composition, induces enhanced lattice distortion or favorable grain boundary characteristics compared to the Nb-containing NbMoTaW composition, leading to higher resistance to plastic deformation.
cross_paper_synthesis.discriminating_experiment: To validate the hypothesis, one would need to perform high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) on both film types to quantify grain size distributions and measure local lattice strains, correlating these microstructural metrics directly to the hardness values to isolate the specific contribution of Cu/V addition versus Nb substitution.
